theme: End-of-Summer Push: Turn the Last Heat of the Season into Next Year's Momentum

linkedin.text:
There's a window at the end of summer that most companies miss.

It's not the holiday party planning season yet. It's not Q4 crunch time yet. It's the two-to-six weeks where decisions made now determine whether your people walk into the final quarter with momentum — or just obligation.

After 16 years and 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations, here's what we see consistently:

The companies whose year-end events land — the ones that move culture, close sales cycles, and generate the internal stories that last — almost always started the conversation in this window. Not in October. Not when venues are already blocked.

The brief is usually one of three things:
→ A Q4 kick-off that reframes the final push as an opportunity, not a sprint
→ A year-end incentive trip that tells top performers their effort was seen
→ A gala or convention that closes the year with weight, not just catering

The logistics difference between a great event and a forgettable one is often just the planning runway.

If any of those are on your radar for Q4 or Q1, I'd genuinely enjoy a 20-minute conversation about what that could look like — no deck, no pitch, just a clear-headed brief.

DM me or drop a comment. Happy to connect.
